sections.h2: How Cabarrus County values and bills a house
sections.html:
Cabarrus County values every parcel at market value as of January 1, then sends one bill that combines the county rate with any city, town and fire district rates that apply to the address. Current values are as of January 1, 2024, and no flat percentage change was applied to prior assessments.

A parcel's value has three building blocks: the land, the building (type, age and physical characteristics) and extras such as garages, sheds, pools, fences and driveways. Improvements under construction are valued partially, based on percent complete on January 1, and those values feed the bill.

State law, G.S. 105-286, allows at most eight years between reappraisals. Cabarrus cut that gap in half so values follow the market more closely.

sections.h2: Who to contact about assessments and appeals
sections.html:
The Tax Administration department handles assessment and appeals, and the Revaluation office answers value questions at 704-920-2126 or revalinfo@cabarruscounty.us. The office is at 65 Church Street S in Concord, NC 28025, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Collections bills and collects for every jurisdiction in the county: the county itself, seven cities or towns and 16 fire districts. The Equalization and Review Board hears appeals, and its members are appointed by the County Commissioners from residents who know the local real estate market.

  • Real estate values and property cards: the county's online real estate search, by name, address or parcel
  • Comparable sales: a map-based comparable sales tool on the Tax Revaluation page
  • Relief programs: homestead, disabled veteran and circuit breaker, plus present use value and wildlife conservation programs
  • Payment plans: the Collections office

sections.h2: How to appeal your Cabarrus County value
sections.html:
Start in writing by asking for an informal review. No particular form is needed, but the more evidence you attach, the stronger the case. The appraiser for your area looks at what you send and responds with an Informal Review notice, which also explains how to go to the formal level.

You get 30 days from that response notice to continue the appeal. A request for a Board of Equalization and Review hearing goes to Cabarrus County Tax Revaluation, PO Box 707, Concord, NC 28026-0707, or through the county's online system. It must reach the Office of the County Assessor within 30 days of the date on your Notice of Real Estate Assessed Value letter, or any time before the Board adjourns, usually in late April and advertised in the local newspaper.

After you submit, you and the county appraiser get one more chance to review the case, and you complete an Application for Hearing form. The board hears evidence from both sides and mails a decision letter within 30 days of the hearing. Owners still unhappy after that can go to the NC Property Tax Commission, and under G.S. 105-290, written notice of that appeal, stating your grounds, must be filed within 30 days of the mailing date on the board's ruling.

The size of the jump between two revaluations is not a valid reason for appeal. Compare your parcel to similar sales instead.

Bills are due September 1 and are past due if not paid before the following January 5. Real estate, business and individual personal property bills are mailed each year in late July or the first days of August.

Cabarrus County tax calendar
WhenWhat happens
January 1Value date for each parcel; the bill goes to the owner on this date
JanuaryPersonal property listing form is available; real estate changes are listed on it
Late AprilBoard of Equalization and Review usually adjourns
By June 30Tax rates set through the budget process

September 1Taxes due
After January 5Bill is delinquent and open to collection or foreclosure

State law sets interest at 2 percent for January 6 to February 1, then three-fourths of one percent a month after that (G.S. 105-360). A delinquent bill faces collection actions or tax foreclosure. Collections will work out a payment plan, but the bill must still be paid in full by the delinquent date, and you have to ask for the plan, ideally early in the year.

The county rate for 2026 is $0.576 per $100 of assessed value, and each city or town and fire district adds its own rate. Kannapolis, for example, adds $0.5595 on top of the county rate for an address inside the city.

Rates are set during the budget process, with the Board of Commissioners and each municipality finishing theirs no later than June 30. A change in assessed value may or may not change your bill, because the effect is unknown until the rates are set. To estimate your own bill, use the county's real estate search for the assessed value and the rate page for each district that covers your parcel, then ask Collections to confirm.

sections.h2: Tax breaks for Cabarrus County homeowners
sections.html:
Homestead, disabled veteran and circuit breaker relief are all filed with the county assessor. Under G.S. 105-277.1, a homeowner aged 65 or over, or one who is totally and permanently disabled, with income below the yearly cap, can shield $25,000 or half the appraised value of the residence, whichever is larger. The cap is $38,800 for 2026.

  • Disabled veterans: the first $45,000 of value is excluded, with no age or income test on the state form
  • Circuit breaker: after five years of owning and living in the home, the bill is capped at 4.0% of income under the cap or 5.0% between the cap and $58,200 (2026), and the excess is deferred as a lien
  • Form AV-9 goes to the assessor, who accepts it until June 1 before the tax year, and no owner may combine the three

Farm, forest and wildlife landowners should also ask about the present use value programs, which the county lists separately with applications.

sections.h2: Who pays the bill when you sell
sections.html:
Have this year's bill paid out of the sale proceeds, in line with G.S. 105-355. The bill is issued in the owner's name as of January 1, so a seller who sold partway through the year should pass the bill on to the buyer.

The county's median owner-occupied home value is $354,800, and 71.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Values in the county's real estate search are set as of January 1, 2024, so compare yours with recent neighborhood sales before you list. Ask the closing attorney for a payoff of all taxes due, including fire district amounts, and ask Collections for the delinquent status of any prior year.

Pull your property card from the real estate search and check the land, building and extras the county has on file. Look at the comparable sales tool to see how nearby homes sold. Ask Collections for the current year's balance and any prior-year delinquency. If you receive homestead or circuit breaker relief, tell your closing attorney, since a deferral can come due. Last, confirm which bill goes to the buyer after closing, because the county issues it to whoever owned the parcel on January 1.

faqs.q: When are Cabarrus County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1. A bill is past due if not paid before the following January 5, and state law starts interest on January 6. Bills are mailed in late July or the first days of August.

faqs.q: How often does Cabarrus County revalue real estate?
faqs.a: Every four years by local choice, although state law only requires every eight. The current values are as of January 1, 2024. The Revaluation office at 704-920-2126 can confirm the next cycle.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Cabarrus County property value?
faqs.a: Submit a written request for an informal review, then appeal to the Board of Equalization and Review within 30 days of your value notice or before the board adjourns, usually in late April. The decision letter arrives within 30 days of the hearing.

faqs.q: Does Cabarrus County allow installments on a tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The Collections office works with taxpayers on payment plans, but you must request one and the bill still has to be paid in full by the delinquent date. Contacting them early in the year is preferred.

faqs.q: Who gets the bill if my Cabarrus County house sells before year end?
faqs.a: The bill still goes out in the name of the owner on January 1, so forward it to the buyer if you receive it after closing. Settle the current year's tax through closing so it does not turn into a lien problem for the new owner.
